corrected_claim: After an update of commercial OCT segmentation software (Heidelberg HRA/Spectralis 5.6.4.0 to 6.0.7.0), a mixed-version scenario (baseline segmented with the old version, follow-up with the new) gave two-year RNFL atrophy of −0.63 μm, against −0.95 μm when both visits used the old version (difference 0.32 μm, p<0.001) and −0.71 μm when both used the new version (0.08 μm, p=0.136; 178 patients); the authors recommended segmenting baseline and follow-up scans with the same software version.
notes: All claim numbers match Section 3.4 of the version of record. The published abstract does not report the longitudinal numbers (it gives 838 scans, 213 MS patients and 61 controls, a +0.16 μm mean offset and individual differences up to 6 μm), so there is no abstract-manuscript conflict. The paper calls the mixed scenario '(hypothetically) most extreme case'; it was computed, not observed from stored data. Internal inconsistency in the version of record: old/old vs new/new is reported as 'This difference of 0.18 μm' although the reported means differ by 0.24 μm; do not quote 0.18.

notes: Only the Japanese translation (JASTRO) was reachable. In it, A1.1.4 says the user must decide whether to install a new version and how much testing to do before clinical release, and that vendors should give enough information for an informed choice without expecting a recommissioning of the whole system; A1.2.5 calls for testing prioritised by that analysis, detailed for changes to MU or dose calculation, beam modelling or anatomy and image input, while other changes may need little testing.
